rows.subtype: Reading a partner's or roommate's unspoken needs [Interpreting]
rows.description: A young adult notices signs such as quietness, irritability or clutter and infers a need for rest or space. These inferences can be wrong, so checking ("Do you want company or quiet?") is wiser than assuming.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult gives feedback to a peer or project member with specific examples and a suggestion. A rebuke in public often produces defensiveness; private, timely and respectful feedback works better.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Taking criticism without shrinking or bristling [Regulating]
rows.description: A young adult listens to feedback, asks clarifying questions and separates useful points from unfair ones. Immediate defence or total self-blame both make learning harder.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Contempt and ridicule as warning signs [Interpreting]
rows.description: A young adult recognises sneering, mockery and eye-rolls in a relationship as signs of disrespect that damage trust. Naming the pattern calmly, setting a limit or seeking help is wiser than trading insults.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, contempt, calm, trust

rows.description: A young adult may face "Do this or I leave" from a friend, partner or family member. Some ultimatums state a real boundary, others are pressure or control; consider whether choices are respected and seek support if fear or coercion is present.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, fear, resentment

rows.subtype: Appeals to emotion, authority and logic [Interpreting]
rows.description: A young adult identifies appeals used in ads, politics and personal requests and weighs evidence. Emotional appeals are not always manipulation, but urgency, fear and flattery deserve extra scrutiny.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Negotiating shared living or study arrangements [Expressing]
rows.description: A young adult negotiates chores, costs and schedules by stating interests, not just positions, and looking for options that serve both sides. Written agreements avoid later disagreement.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult shares family stories, cultural background and personal milestones to be known. What to disclose is a personal choice, and no one is obliged to reveal private details, including identity, before feeling safe.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult shares fears, history or hopes gradually with friends or partners and watches for reciprocity. Trust grows through matched, gradual sharing; sharing too much too soon can leave one feeling exposed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, hope, trust

rows.description: A young adult says "It was slightly damp" after a flood or "Not my best day" after a disaster. Understatement conveys coping and irony, and it depends on shared understanding of the true scale.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
